name: Jack Sim
method: Muse Spark web search (3 calls) for leads; every fact below re-read from the cited page by the agent. corroborated = two or more independent sources.

facts.text: Born in 1957 into a poor family; he describes the place as 'a slum in Singapore', and CNA as 'poverty-stricken Singapore'.
facts.quote: I was born in a slum in Singapore in 1957.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)
CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: He was the second of three children; the family lived in an impoverished village in Upper Serangoon with no plumbing.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: His father was a grocery/provision-shop assistant whose pay 'could hardly feed his family': three children, their mother and a grandmother.
facts.quote: My father worked in a grocery shop and his salary as a shop assistant could hardly feed his family
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)
CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: The family often could not afford clothes and depended on donated ones.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: Home was an attap house with the toilet outside and water from a shared standpipe; there was water rationing and outbreaks of cholera and typhoid.
facts.quote: Life was in an attap house and … the toilet was outside.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim (CNA, 2019)

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
Tatler Asia, Impact List 2020 profile

facts.text: The kampong toilet was a bucket system in an outhouse; he remembers typhoid, cholera and intestinal worms.
facts.quote: We didn't have a toilet in the house, but a bucket system in the outhouse
facts.speaker: Jack Sim (Tatler Asia, 2020)

sources.label: Tatler Asia, Impact List 2020 profile
CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: His mother, Tan Siam Kheng, first tried selling pancakes through a neighbour's fruit pushcart; it failed, and she gave the pancakes away to neighbours for three nights.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: With her last dollar she took a smocking-cushion class at the community centre, then taught six neighbours the same lesson for a dollar each, a five-dollar profit.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: She bought blank exercise books at 10 cents each; Jack, his brother and sister hand-copied her designs into pattern books she sold for two dollars.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: When smocking went out of fashion, she let the make-up girls at CK Tang make her up, memorised the sequence, practised on Jack's sister and the next morning declared herself a wedding beautician.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)
Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: Over about 25 years his mother prepared more than 3,000 brides; she could not read or write, so his brother kept her accounts.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: Jack and his brother took the bus to Chulia Street to buy cosmetics wholesale, and repacked tubs of Nivea into small pots sold as 'Pearl Cream'.

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: He calls his mother's trade his first school, which he 'attended' from age six.
facts.quote: I was glad to begin attending “Mother's Business School” at the age of six.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: Jack Sim, 'Social Entrepreneurship in 1960s Singapore: The Story of My Mother', Skoll (29 Jun 2015)

facts.text: At school he was talkative and restless, was repeatedly sent to stand outside the classroom, and missed lessons; free textbooks did not arrive until April.
facts.quote: The teacher always asked me to stand outside the classroom, so that was why I always failed.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim (CNA, 2019)

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
Unlocking ADHD, 'ADHD Stories: Jack Sim' (2025)

facts.text: He failed his O-levels; two years later, in 1975, he graduated from vocational school with a hotel-management certificate.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: On his brother's advice he went into construction as a site supervisor and was bad at it; the foreman asked his boss to take him off the site.
facts.quote: I supervised construction workers, but I didn't know how to do this job, so my work was really shabby
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: He moved into selling building materials, became his department's top salesman, and an investor persuaded him to start his own company.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: He founded Besco Building Supplies; he could not read accounts and only learned cash had run out when the bank called about a bounced cheque.
facts.quote: We only knew that we ran out of money when the bank called us to say our cheque bounced.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: He under-priced a Raffles City tender by S$1.1 million; after a week of worry he confessed the error to the owners, who gave him the contract at the higher price if he used a German manufacturer.
facts.quote: just started business and immediately going bankrupt?
facts.speaker: Jack Sim, recalling the week

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: In what he calls 'blissful ignorance' he formed a consortium to buy a S$30 million brick factory across the Causeway, then built 14 terrace houses at Rosyth Terrace and a 28-unit block on Meyer Road; he was a millionaire at 29.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: His first marriage, in 1989, ended in divorce after a year; he remarried in 1990 and has four children (two sons, two daughters).

sources.label: Wikipedia: Jack Sim

The Pride (Singapore Kindness Movement), 11 Jan 2018

facts.text: His French roof-tile supplier offered a joint clay-tile factory in Malaysia; he persuaded developers the Mediterranean look would raise prices, and within three years the firm dominated the market.
facts.quote: Your house will sell (for) a higher price if it looks like that
facts.speaker: Jack Sim to developers

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: The Asian financial crisis forced him to retrench staff and halved the value of his 15 properties; he held on.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: A speech by then-Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, saying a society's graciousness could be measured by the cleanliness of its toilets, set him on toilets as a cause.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)
The Pride (Singapore Kindness Movement), 11 Jan 2018
Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: Staff and peers called the toilet idea 'crazy'; he told them social work made him feel useful when the office made him feel like a failure.
facts.quote: When I come to the office, I don't feel useful. I feel like a failure.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: He told his wife that after the recession he would quit business for social work 'because it's so much more fulfilling'.

sources.label: CNA Insider, 'From O-level failure to millionaire at 29, on a policy of honesty first' (2019)

facts.text: In December 1998 he founded the Restroom Association of Singapore; its 'Happy Toilet' award was his idea.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Jack Sim

facts.text: He paid $2,000 for Rediffusion's dialect audio archive at Hillview before the building was demolished, with one day to collect it; he later donated over 4,700 reels to the National Archives.
facts.quote: You can have everything you want for $2,000.
facts.speaker: a Rediffusion contact, as Sim recalled in a 2012 oral history

facts.text: Talking about toilets was taboo and people laughed at him; he made toilet humour his brand and became 'Mr Toilet'.
facts.quote: We go to the toilet six to eight times a day and spend three full years of our lives inside the toilet
facts.speaker: Jack Sim (Tatler Asia, 2020)

facts.quote: There is nothing wrong with going to the toilet.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim (Eco-Business, Jul 2013)

facts.text: At 60 he told The Pride that Singapore's toilets compare with Japan's and should be praised.
facts.quote: I think Singaporeans don't know how good we have it.
facts.speaker: Jack Sim

sources.label: The Pride (Singapore Kindness Movement), 11 Jan 2018
